parole.significato: A slim hardwood spear or javelin with an iron tip, especially those used by Bantu peoples of Southern Africa.
parole.testo: From French azagaie (now zagaie) or Portuguese azagaia, Spanish azagaya, and later in the forms that have become most common borrowed from Afrikaans assegaai, from colloquial Arabic اَلزَّغَايَة (az-zaḡāya), from Proto-Berber *zaġāya (“spear”).

parole.significato: Ornate, intricate, decorated, laden with detail.
parole.testo: Via French baroque (which originally meant a pearl of irregular shape), from Portuguese barroco (“irregular pearl”); related to Spanish barrueco and Italian barocco, of uncertain ultimate origin, but possibly from Latin verrūca (“wart”). parole.significato: A Hindu dancing-girl.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French bayadère, from Portuguese bailadeira, from bailar (“to dance”).

parole.significato: A Buddhist monk or priest in East Asia.
parole.testo: From French bonze, from Portuguese bonzo, from Japanese 凡僧 (bonzō), from Middle Chinese 凡 (bjom, “ordinary”) + 僧 (song, “Buddhist monk”).

parole.significato: The sperm whale, Physeter macrocephalus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French cachalot, from Portuguese cachalote, from cachola (“head”) + -ote.

parole.significato: A sweet eaten to sweeten the breath.
parole.testo: From French cachou, from Portuguese cachu, from Malay kacu (“type of acacia”).

parole.significato: An alloy of lead and tin, from the Far East.
parole.testo: From French calin, calain, from Portuguese calaim, from Arabic قَلَعِيّ (qalaʕiyy).

parole.significato: A sheep of a domesticated breed from West Africa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French Cameroun, from Portuguese Rio dos Camarões (“river of prawns”), a name given to the Wouri river estuary, in 1472 by the sailors of the Portuguese explorer Fernão do Pó (a.k.a. parole.significato: A heavy wooden collar or yoke borne on the shoulders and enclosing the neck and arms, formerly used in East Asia to pun…
parole.testo: From French cangue, from Portuguese canga.

parole.significato: Synonym of Cochin (“type of domestic hen”).
parole.testo: From French Cochin-China; from a Portuguese corruption of Ko-chen, + China, distinguishing it from the Indian town of Cochin (which has a different etymology and was a Portuguese colony).

parole.significato: A wild feline, of species Puma concolor, native to the Americas.
parole.testo: From French couguar, from Portuguese cuguardo, a deformation of Brazilian Portuguese suçuarana (earlier çuçuarana), from Old Tupi sûasuarana.

parole.significato: One of several species of armadillo of the genera Dasypus and Euphractus, with five toes on both the fore and the hind…
parole.testo: From French encoubert, from Portuguese encorberto, encuberto (“covered”).

parole.significato: Something which is believed to possess, contain, or cause spiritual or magical powers; an amulet or a talisman.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French fétiche, from Portuguese feitiço, from Latin factīcius (“artificial”). Doublet of factitious.

parole.significato: A glossy, resinous material used as a surface coating; either a natural exudation of certain trees, or a solution of ni…
parole.testo: Borrowed from French lacque (“a sort of sealing wax”), from Portuguese laca, lacca (“gum lac”), from Persian لاک (lâk), from Hindi लाख (lākh), from Sanskrit लाक्षा (lākṣā). Doublet of lac.

parole.significato: Any of a group of Old World monkeys of the genus Macaca.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from French macaque, from Portuguese macaco, of uncertain origin (see macaco for more). Doublet of macaco.

parole.significato: The tropical plant Manihot esculenta, from which tapioca is prepared; cassava, yuca.
parole.testo: From French manioc, through Portuguese mandioca, ultimately from Old Tupi mani'oka. Doublet of manihot.

parole.significato: Restructuring.
parole.testo: Mistranslation by non-native speakers, based on their native languages’ equivalent terms. These include, but are not limited to, French restructuration, Portuguese reestruturação, and Spanish reestructuración. Likely independently reformed various times.

parole.significato: A medium-sized African wild cat, Leptailurus serval, formerly Felis serval.
parole.testo: From French serval, from Portuguese (lobo) cerval (“Iberian lynx”), from Latin lupus cervārius (literally “stag wolf”), i.e. "wolf that hunts stags", from cervus (“deer, stag”).

parole.significato: A monkey from one of two species of Old World monkeys, of the genus Miopithecus, distinguished by a short-snouted head…
parole.testo: From French talapoin, from Portuguese talapão, from Mon တၠဳ ပိုဲ (tloe poi, “our lord”).

parole.significato: crude zinc
parole.testo: From French toutenague, from Portuguese tutenaga, tutanaga, from Tamil துத்தநாகம் (tuttanākam, “raw zinc”). Doublet of tutty.
